note: Singapore, read on the Ministry of Manpower's and the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority's own pages on 2026-10-30. The Overseas Networks & Expertise Pass is for top talent in business, arts and culture, sports, academia and research (a fixed monthly salary of S$30,000, or outstanding achievements in a sector); it lets its holder start, operate and work for several companies at once and change jobs without a new pass (read as work: any); S$105 on application and S$225 on issue (S$330 kept), within 4 weeks for most cases, up to 5 years and renewable for up to 5. The Employment Pass is for professionals, managers, executives and technicians with a salary from S$5,600 a month and a job the employer applied for (read as work for the sponsor); the same S$105 and S$225; within 10 working days for a Singapore-registered employer and 6 weeks for one without (6 weeks kept, the longer); up to 2 years first and up to 3 on renewal (2 kept as the first grant). Candidates need not be in Singapore when the employer applies, so both are 'either'. Holders of an Employment Pass may apply for permanent residence with no sponsor; no number of years is stated, so none is kept. Permanent residence: S$100 on application and S$20 for the entry permit on completing formalities (S$120 kept; the 5-year re-entry permit, S$50, and the identity card, S$50, are separate), within 6 months for most. Citizenship is open to a permanent resident of at least 2 years aged 21 or over, so permanent residence's years count; the pages read don't say that years on a pass count, so the passes aren't marked. A 5-year Employment Pass for experienced tech professionals in shortage isn't a performer's and isn't written.
